extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists and zoologists studying freshwater sponges (Spongillidae); museum curators and naturalists preparing species descriptions and identifications
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and applying morphological diagnostic criteria and keys for genera and species of freshwater sponges (Spongillidae) in the Indian region, using characters of skeleton, spicules, gemmules, and habit. Includes species descriptions, distribution, habitat notes, and comparative measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of spicule and microsclere morphology as primary generic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The genus is distinguished by the nature of the free microscleres, the microscleres of the gemmule being similar in the two genera. The free microscleres consist as a rule of several or many shafts meeting together in several or many planes at a common centre, which is usually nodular. The free ends of these shafts often possess rudimentary rotulæ. Occasionally a free microsclere may be found that is a true monaxon and sometimes such spicules are more or less distinctly birotulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare presence/absence, number of shafts, central nodule, rotulae (rudimentary vs developed), and occurrence of monaxons or birotulates; these micro-sclere characters are highlighted as the key to distinguishing Dosilia from Ephydatia and other genera. Examples and caveats: some species show intermediate characters and may require new genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton architecture as diagnostic (radiating vs reticulate; feathery vs compact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The skeleton consists mainly of radiating fibres which bifurcate frequently in such a way that a bush-like structure is produced. Transverse fibres are very feebly developed and are invisible to the naked eye. Owing to the structure of the skeleton the sponge has a feathery appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate degree of radiating fibres, frequency of bifurcation, development of transverse fibres, presence/absence of spongin, and overall appearance (feathery, reticulate, dense, almost structureless). Skeleton structure is cited repeatedly to separate genera and species (e.g., Dosilia's bush-like structure vs Tubella's reticulate, Trochospongilla's dense reticulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule-spicule rotulae shape and edge (smooth vs serrated) as generic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic feature of this genus is that the rotulæ of the gemmule-spicules, which are homogeneous, have smooth instead of serrated edges. Their stem is always short and they are usually embedded in a granular pneumatic coat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rotula edge sculpture (smooth, serrated, undulated/nodulose), equality or inequality of upper and lower rotulae, and stem length to decide generic placement (Trochospongilla vs Ephydatia vs Tubella). Note exceptions and intermediate conditions in some species (e.g., Australian Ephydatia capewelli).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality/inequality of upper and lower rotulae (birotulate condition) for species separation
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Rotules of the gemmule-spicules equal or nearly so. II. Upper rotule of the gemmule-spicules distinctly smaller than the lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in the key to Indian Trochospongilla: if rotulæ equal → check skeleton-spicule surface (smooth → latouchiana; spiny blunt → phillottiana). If upper rotula smaller → pennsylvanica (skeleton-spicules spiny, pointed). Measure relative diameters of rotulæ and shaft-to-rotula proportions to discriminate species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton-spicule surface ornamentation (smooth vs spiny; shape and proportions) as species-level metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton-spicules smooth, usually pointed ... Skeleton-spicules spiny, blunt ... Skeleton-spicules slender, cylindrical, almost straight, sharp or blunt, minutely, uniformly or almost uniformly spined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether skeleton-spicules are smooth or bear spines, their tip shape (pointed vs blunt), curvature, and length:breadth ratios (often ~20:1). These metrics recur in species diagnoses (e.g., T. latouchiana smooth and slender; T. phillottiana spiny and blunt; T. pennsylvanica minutely spined). Use micrometres/measurements when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule morphology and arrangement (size, shape, coat, foraminal tubule, position in sponge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules small (0.2 × 0.18 mm.), as a rule very numerous and scattered throughout the sponge, flask-shaped, clothed when mature with a thin microcell coat ... Gemmules numerous, situated at the base of the sponge in irregular, one-layered patches, small (0.32 × 0.264 mm.), of a brilliant golden colour, distinctly wider than high, with a single aperture situated on an eminence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record gemmule size, shape (spherical, flask-shaped, depressed), number and distribution (throughout sponge vs at base), presence/absence and thickness of pneumatic/microcell coat, foraminal tubule shape (short, funnel-shaped), and whether gemmules are enclosed in cages of skeleton-spicules. These characters are used to separate species and to explain ecological behaviors (e.g., buoyancy, dispersal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence/absence and form of flesh-spicules (microstrongyles, amphioxous, birotulates) as diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Flesh-spicules occasionally amphioxous or birotulate and with a single shaft, more frequently consisting of many shafts meeting in a distinct central nodule, which is itself smooth; the shafts irregularly spiny ... No flesh-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document whether flesh-spicules occur, their structure (single shaft vs multiple shafts with central nodule), spination, and relative proportions. Presence/absence and morphology of flesh-spicules help distinguish species and indicate relationships among genera (e.g., Dosilia has characteristic free microscleres; some species lack flesh-spicules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quantitative measurements (micrometric averages) for identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Average Measurements. Diameter of gemmule 0.2 × 0.18 mm. Length of skeleton-spicule 0.28". Length of birotulate-spicule 0.175". Diameter of rotula 0.02" ... Comparison table of Travancore and Pennsylvania specimens giving lengths and breadths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise measurements (length and breadth of skeleton-spicule, length of birotulate/gemmule-spicule, diameter of rotula and gemmule) and averages for comparison between specimens/regions. Use ranges and averages to assess conspecificity or regional variation; tables comparing populations (e.g., Travancore vs Pennsylvania) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponge habit and macromorphology (form, colour, thickness, oscula) as field diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forming cushion-shaped masses rarely more than a few centimetres in diameter or thickness and of a brown or yellow colour, hard but rather brittle; surface evenly rounded, minutely hispid; oscula inconspicuous, small, circular, depressed, very few in number ... Sponge forming sheets or patches often of great extent but never more than about 5 mm. thick; the surface minutely hispid, flat; colour pale yellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record overall growth form (cushion, sheet, crust), colour in life/dry, surface texture (hispid, lobe-like projections), thickness, and ostia/oscula characteristics (number, prominence). These macromorphological characters provide useful preliminary separation in the field and are correlated with microcharacters in species descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecological and biological notes as supporting diagnostic information
rubrics_metrics.description: My experience agrees with Carter's, that this species is never found on floating objects but always on stones or brickwork. It grows in the Calcutta 'tanks' on artificial stonework at the edge of the water ... It flourishes during the cold weather and often occupies the same position in succeeding years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record substrate (stones, brickwork, water-plant roots, logs), seasonal occurrence (monsoon, cold weather), flotation behavior (floating after rains due to gas), and associations with other sponges or incolæ (e.g., Sisyra indica larva). Use ecological data to interpret gemmule dispersal, persistence, and habitat specificity; such notes often corroborate morphological identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dosilia genus diagnosis (as given)
rubrics_metrics.description: This genus is distinguished from Ephydatia by the nature of the free microscleres, the microscleres of the gemmule being similar in the two genera. The free microscleres consist as a rule of several or many shafts meeting together in several or many planes at a common centre, which is usually nodular. The free ends of these shafts often possess rudimentary rotulæ. Occasionally a free microsclere may be found that is a true monaxon and sometimes such spicules are more or less distinctly birotulate. The skeleton is also characteristic. It consists mainly of radiating fibres which bifurcate frequently in such a way that a bush-like structure is produced. Transverse fibres are very feebly developed and are invisible to the naked eye. Owing to the structure of the skeleton the sponge has a feathery appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate forms described as varieties (palmeri, brouini) with Dosilia plumosa unless clear differences warrant species status; note that species with similar free microscleres but different gemmule-spicules may need new genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dosilia plumosa species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forming soft irregular masses sometimes as much as 14 cm. in diameter, pale brown or brilliant green; surface covered with irregular projections usually of a lobe-like nature. Skeleton delicate, branches diverging widely, containing considerable chitin. Skeleton-spicules smooth, sharply pointed, nearly straight, moderately slender, about twenty times as long as their greatest transverse diameter. Flesh-spicules occasionally amphioxous or birotulate; gemmule-spicules with long, slender, straight shafts bearing short horizontal spines; rotulæ distinctly convex in profile; shafts not extending beyond disks. Gemmules somewhat depressed, covered with a thick granular pneumatic coat, single aperture depressed; each gemmule surrounded by a circle or several circles of flesh-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note habit (floating vs attached), tendency to be more resistant/coarse than other species, seasonal appearance (after monsoon rains), and possible confusion with other taxa (e.g., S. lacustris subspecies). TYPE and locality information provided; use both micro- and macromorphology plus habitat for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trochospongilla genus circumscription
rubrics_metrics.description: The rotulæ of the gemmule-spicules, which are homogeneous, have smooth instead of serrated edges. Their stem is always short and they are usually embedded in a granular pneumatic coat. The sponge is small in most of the species as yet known; in some species microscleres without rotulæ are associated with the gemmules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in the genus those species in which all gemmule-spicules are birotulate with smooth-edged disks; distinguish from Tubella (upper rotula reduced to a knob) and note rare intermediate conditions. Use rotula edge and stem length as primary generic characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trochospongilla latouchiana species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forming cushion-shaped masses rarely more than a few centimetres in diameter or thickness, brown or yellow, hard but brittle; surface minutely hispid; skeleton dense forming a close reticulation; radiating fibres slender. Skeleton-spicules smooth, about twenty times as long as diameter, usually sharply pointed. No flesh-spicules. Gemmule-spicules with rotulæ circular or slightly asymmetrical, flat or nearly flat, marked with a distinct double circle as seen from above; shaft not projecting beyond them; diameter of rotula 4.5–5 times that of the shaft. Gemmules small (0.2 × 0.18 mm.), numerous, flask-shaped, clothed when mature with a thin microcell coat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combination of smooth skeleton-spicules, absence of flesh-spicules, small flask-shaped gemmules with overlapping birotulates, and provided metrics (skeleton-spicule length, birotulate length, rotula diameter) to identify T. latouchiana and to differentiate it from T. leidyi and other congeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trochospongilla phillottiana species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge hard but friable forming sheets or patches often of great extent but never more than about 5 mm. thick; surface minutely hispid; colour pale yellow; oscula inconspicuous. Skeleton dense but produced mainly by single spicules forming triangular meshes; each gemmule enclosed in an open irregular cage of skeleton-spicules. Skeleton-spicules short, slender, blunt, regularly and strongly spiny. No flesh-spicules. Gemmules numerous, at base in irregular patches, small (0.32 × 0.264 mm.), clothed with pneumatic coat containing relatively large irregular air-spaces; rotulæ circular, very wide compared with shaft, concave on surface; shaft projecting as an umbo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish by strongly spined, blunt skeleton-spicules and gemmule features (large rotulæ, golden-coloured gemmules in basal patches), plus the structure of gemmule cages. Measurements given for spicules and gemmules should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trochospongilla pennsylvanica species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge soft, fragile forming small cushion-shaped masses, grey or green; skeleton close, almost structureless. Skeleton-spicules slender, cylindrical, almost straight, sharp or blunt, minutely, uniformly or almost uniformly spined; no flesh-spicules. Gemmule-spicules with the lower rotula invariably larger than the upper; both rotulæ flat or somewhat sinuous in profile, usually circular but sometimes asymmetrical; gemmules small, numerous or altogether absent, covered with granular pneumatic coat of variable thickness; rotulæ of gemmule-spicules overlapping and sometimes projecting out of the granular coat. Comparative measurements given (Travancore vs Pennsylvania).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the unequal rotulæ (lower > upper), minutely spined skeleton-spicules, and comparative metric ranges to identify T. pennsylvanica and to consider geographic variation between specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tubella genus diagnosis (birotulate asymmetry; 'little trumpet')
rubrics_metrics.description: This genus is distinguished from Ephydatia and Trochospongilla by the fact that the two ends of the gemmule-spicules are unlike not only in size but also in form. It sometimes happens that this unlikeness is not so marked in some spicules as in others, but in some if not in all the upper end of the shaft is reduced to a rounded knob, while the lower end expands into a flat transverse disk with a smooth or denticulated edge. The spicule thus resembles a little trumpet resting on its mouth. The shaft is generally slender and of considerable length. The skeleton is as a rule distinctly reticulate and often hard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary diagnostic character is the asymmetric birotulate spicule (upper reduced to knob, lower expanded disk). Combine with reticulate, often hard skeleton and the proportions of skeleton-spicules to place species in Tubella rather than Trochospongilla or Ephydatia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tubella vesparioides species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forming rather thick sheets of considerable size, hard but brittle, almost black in colour; external membrane supported on a reticulate horizontal skeleton. Surface covered with network of stout spicule-fibres with vertical sharp fibres at nodes; skeleton pervaded by a network of parallel spicules overlapping at ends and bound by profuse spongin. Skeleton-spicules slender, smooth, amphioxous, bent in a wide arc or at an angle. Gemmule-spicules terminating above in a rounded, knob-like structure and below in a relatively broad, flat rotula very deeply and irregularly indented; shaft projecting slightly below the rotula, long, slender, generally armed with a few stout conical spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish from related Tubella vesparium by smooth skeleton-spicules and deeply indented disk of gemmule-spicules; use given average measurements for spicule lengths and rotula/ gemmule diameters and note habitat (grown on submerged logs/branches, found dry in March).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corvospongilla genus diagnosis (absence of rotulæ on gemmule-spicules; recurved-spined flesh-spicules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spongillidæ in which the gemmule-spicules are without a trace of rotulæ and the flesh-spicules have slender cylindrical shafts that bear at or near either end a circle of strong recurved spines. The gemmule-spicules are usually stout and sausage-shaped, and the gemmules resemble those of Stratospongilla in structure. The skeleton is strong and the skeleton-spicules stout, both resembling those of the 'genus' Potamolepis, Marshall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key generic characters: gemmule-spicules lacking rotulæ, flesh-spicules with rings of recurved spines, stout skeleton-spicules and strong skeleton. Note geographic concentration in Africa and the Oriental Region and the possibility of similar/connecting taxa (Potts' forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key to Indian Corvospongilla species (gemmule layer size relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Gemmule with two layers of gemmule-spicules; those of the inner layer not markedly smaller than those of the outer. II. Gemmule with two layers of gemmule-spicules, the outer of which contains spicules of much greater size than the inner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use number of layers and relative size differences between inner and outer gemmule-spicule layers to separate C. burmanica (inner not markedly smaller) from C. lapidosa (outer much larger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corvospongilla burmanica species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forming a shallow sheet, hard, not very strong, pale brownish; surface irregularly spiny; oscula small but conspicuous. Skeleton dense but not regular; network composed largely of single spines; thick radiating fibres distinguishable in upper part. Skeleton-spicules smooth, not very stout, amphistrongylous, occasionally swollen at the ends, measuring about 0.27 × 0.0195 mm. Flesh-spicules with distinct rotules, recurved spines numbering 4 to 6, measuring about 1/7 the length of the spicules; gemmule-spicules amphioxous, distinctly curved, covered sparsely with fine spines; gemmules strongly adherent, arranged in small groups, single or double, each covered by two layers of gemmule-spicules bound together in chitinous substance; foraminal tubule short, cylindrical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify by combination of dense skeleton of single spines, presence of flesh-spicules with 4–6 recurved spines, and gemmules covered by two layers of gemmule-spicules (inner and outer) with cages of skeleton-spicules externally; habitat notes provided (Myitkyo, Pegu-Sittang canal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corvospongilla lapidosa species diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge forms a thin but extremely hard and resistant crust, surface level, slightly concave, or distinctly corrugated; occasional projecting spicule groups; dermal membrane adheres closely. Skeleton extremely dense, almost structureless; broad vertical groups of spicules occur but lack spongin. Skeleton-spicules sausage-shaped, often swollen at the ends or constricted in middle; many twisted or bent, majority smooth. Flesh-spicules vary in length with shafts ~0.159 mm. or ~0.05 mm.; birotulate rotula shafts average 0.0026 mm. diameter and rotula 0.0106 mm., rotula consisting of 6–8 spines. Gemmule-spicules vary greatly in size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish by extraordinarily hard crusty habit, extremely dense interlocking skeleton, sausage-shaped skeleton-spicules, large variability in flesh- and gemmule-spicule sizes, and precise shaft/rotula metrics when available.
